title: L.A. Confidential
tagline: Off the record, on the QT, and very hush-hush.
about: Three LAPD cops in 1953 Los Angeles dig into a coffee shop massacre, and the trail leads straight back into their own department.

Crisp rolls, pork and cabbage, Chinese mustard.How to make it300g pork mince2 cups wombok, finely shredded1 carrot, grated3 spring onions, sliced1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated2 tbsp soy sauce1 tsp sesame oil12 spring rolls of wrappers1 L vegetable oil, for frying2 tbsp hot English mustard powderStir-fry the pork until browned, add the wombok, carrot, spring onion and ginger and cook until wilted, then season with the soy and sesame oil and cool.Lay out a wrapper, add a spoon of filling, fold in the sides and roll up tightly, sealing with a dab of water.Mix the mustard powder with a little cold water to a smooth, hot paste.Fry the rolls in oil at 180°C in batches until deep golden, then drain.Serve hot with the mustard.Frolic Room devilled eggs with paprikaJack leaves his payola as a tip. Creamy yolks, mustard, cayenne, chives.How to make it6 eggs3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 tsp Dijon mustard1 tsp white vinegar1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1 tsp sweet paprika1 tbsp chopped chivesLower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water.Peel, halve lengthways and tip the yolks into a bowl.Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, cayenne and a pinch of salt until smooth.Pipe or spoon back into the whites, dust with paprika and top with chives.Salted crackers and dill picklesOff the record, and very hush-hush.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Blue PlatesNite Owl chilli size with onions and cheddarExley takes the call to the Nite Owl. Grilled patty under beef chilli, cheese, onion.How to make it1kg beef mince1 brown onion, diced3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp chilli powder2 tsp ground cumin400g tin crushed tomatoes400g tin kidney beans, drained250ml beef stock4 thick slices of white bread, toasted120g cheddar, grated1/2 white onion, finely dicedBrown 400g of the mince with the onion and garlic, then add the chilli powder and cumin.Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer until thick and dark.Shape the rest of the mince into 4 thick patties, season and grill or pan-fry until browned and just cooked.Put each patty on a slice of toast, ladle over the chilli and top with cheddar and raw onion.Ghost of Christmas Past ham steak with grilled pineappleBud pulls Santa's sleigh off the roof. Brown sugar glaze, pineapple, buttered greens.How to make it4 thick ham steaks3 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp Dijon mustard1 tbsp apple cider vinegar1/2 tsp ground cloves4 fresh pineapple rings300g green beans30g butter600g small potatoesBoil the potatoes until tender, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes, then drain and toss with the butter.Mix the sugar, mustard, vinegar and cloves into a glaze.Sear the ham steaks in a hot pan, brush with glaze and turn until sticky and caramelised.Grill the pineapple in the same pan until charred, and serve on the ham with the potatoes and beans.Pie and SweetsRollo Tomasi's cherry pie a la modeRollo Tomasi, the one who got away. Lattice cherry pie, vanilla ice cream.How to make it2 sheets of frozen shortcrust pastry, thawed2 x 680g jars of pitted morello cherries, drained, 125ml juice kept100g caster sugar3 tbsp cornflour1 lemon, juiced1/2 tsp almond essence1 egg, beaten4 scoops of vanilla ice creamLine a 22cm pie dish with one sheet of pastry and chill.Warm the cherries, kept juice, sugar, cornflour and lemon juice, stirring, until thick and glossy, then stir in the almond and cool.Fill the pie, cut the second sheet into strips and weave a lattice over the top, then brush with egg.Bake at 200°C until the pastry is deep golden and the filling bubbles.Cool a little and serve warm with ice cream.Coffee and RyeAll the whiskey in Ireland coffeeDudley wouldn't trade places with Exley. Hot coffee, Irish whiskey, brown sugar, cream.How to make it600ml strong hot coffee160ml Irish whiskey4 tsp brown sugar150ml thickened creamWarm 4 glasses with hot water, then tip it out.Stir a teaspoon of sugar and 40ml whiskey into each, then fill with coffee.Lightly whip the cream and float it over the back of a spoon.Rye and soda in a motel glassTwo fingers, no ice, no questions.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
